analysis: The only change in docs/developer/test.md is at head lines 1049-1050, a documentation edit that updates the release SDK qualification text from SDK 27 / Swift 6.4 to SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 (Xcode 27.2) and adds a link to build.md#sdk-27-release-builds-and-caches. The supplied units (head lines 1837-2766) are unchanged surrounding test documentation. I reviewed them against the threat model, including the T-041 prefix-cache/SSD tier and the TB-011 App Attest, TB-012 and TB-013 boundaries. No code, configuration, key handling, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-policy behavior changes. The prefix-cache test instructions still describe ephemeral or test-owned roots, a non-persistent test key and cache policies off, which is consistent with T-041 and weakens nothing. The documented live and opt-in tests use env-gated, loopback, owner-owned paths, and the docs say not to send tokens, prompts or completions to telemetry. Nothing contradicts the threat model or invalidates its assumptions. Remaining integration question: the actual toolchain change (SDK 27.2, Xcode 27.2) lives in workflows or build files outside this batch. Whether it affects signed-artifact qualification (T-054, A-017) would need review of those files, but this doc edit alone does not create a security regression.
